scenario: AITA For telling my Girlfriend she needs to quit whining about who eats what or I'll kick her out | Well, the title says it all, the past few weeks have both been really great and extremely infuriating. We don't live together, but we decided it would be best to stick together during these times as we have no family near as such she is staying with me as I have my own apartment and she has multiple roommates hence the choice. Well she eats more then any person I have ever known, especially considering her physical appearance, she is 5'4, petite, thin and yet she eats more than I do and I am 6'6 and a bit of a gymbro. To put it in to perspective, our food bill each week is roughly three times compared to what I usually spend alone. Yet she seems extremely selfconcious about this and as a result will act surprised when something is gone, try to blame me, states I am eating too much whenever I eat anything, essentially, she tries to deflect her eating habits and projects them on to me out of embarrassment about her eating so much I guess? The thing is, I don't care about her eating habits, she can eat whatever she wants to eat what I am done with is her constantly trying to blame me, whining about food and picking fights about it. I talked to her about it multiple times, argued with her about it multiple times but earlier today I just got so tired of another comment, this time brought on by me making a sandwhich at 2 PM when I had eaten at 10 AM I know right, horrible. So I told her that this crap was either going to stop right here and now or I'll kick her out and she can spend the coming weeks or months at her own place. She just started crying, called me horrible and locked herself in the bathroom. At this point I just dont get it anymore, am I being TA here or is she TA?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the guy in this situation is being "AITA" or "Am I the Asshole." The scenario is that he's been living with his girlfriend for a while, and they've been having issues with her eating habits. She eats a lot more than he does, even though she's petite, and this is causing their food bills to skyrocket. He's gotten really frustrated with her because she doesn't just eat a lot but also tries to blame him for the food shortages and argues about it constantly. He's tried talking to her about it multiple times, but nothing seems to change. Finally, he snapped and told her that if she doesn't stop whining about the food, he'll kick her out. She got upset, cried, and locked herself in the bathroom. So, is he being the asshole here? Let's break this down. First, I need to understand both sides of the story. On one hand, he's frustrated because her eating habits are costing him a lot of money, and she's not taking responsibility for it. She's blaming him instead of acknowledging her own behavior. That must be really annoying and stressful, especially if they're living together and sharing expenses. It's understandable that he would get upset about that. On the other hand, he's reacting by threatening to kick her out, which seems pretty harsh. Even if her behavior is annoying, threatening to end the relationship over something like this might be overreacting. It's important to communicate feelings without resorting to threats, especially in a relationship where both people are trying to work things out. I also wonder about the context of their relationship. Are they living together because of necessity, like due to the pandemic or lack of family support? If that's the case, threatening to kick her out might have more serious implications because she might not have anywhere else to go. That could add another layer of stress to the situation. Another thing to consider is whether he's tried other ways to address the issue besides just talking about it. Maybe they could sit down together and find a solution, like setting a budget for groceries or finding a way to split the costs more fairly. If he's only been talking to her about it without any progress, maybe he needs to approach the conversation differently or seek some external help, like couples counseling. It's also worth thinking about why she's acting the way she is. She might be embarrassed about her eating habits, which is why she's deflecting blame onto him. Understanding her perspective could help him approach the situation with more empathy instead of frustration. In the end, while it's understandable that he's frustrated, threatening to kick her out might not be the best way to handle the situation. It could escalate things and damage their relationship further. Finding a more constructive way to communicate and work together to solve the problem would probably be a better approach.
